name: Crizac Ltd
tagline: Asset-light, cash-rich B2B international-student-recruitment platform with elite return ratios -- but management has guided FY27 flat on visa/geopolitical headwinds, so the growth engine has stalled
business_overview: Crizac operates a B2B education platform connecting ~10,000+ recruitment agents to 170+ overseas universities (heavily UK, plus Canada, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand). It earns a percentage of the first-year tuition fee for each enrolled student. ~70% of revenue passes through to agents as commission; adjusted EBITDA margin ~22-25%. Headquartered in Kolkata with co-operations in London.
fundamentals_table: FY26 revenue ~Rs 1,042 Cr, +22.7% YoY; 5-yr revenue CAGR ~57%
Flattish -- management cites Middle-East crisis and US/UK anti-immigration policy
Debt-free; net cash ~Rs 467 Cr; dividend yield ~4.7%
fundamentals_narrative: The financial model is outstanding on paper -- negligible capital employed, ~57% ROE, debt-free, throwing off cash and paying a ~4.7% yield. But the entire thesis is a growth thesis (there is no margin-expansion lever -- agent commissions are a fixed ~70% of revenue), and growth has just been guided to zero for FY27 because international-student flows into Crizac's core UK/Canada/Australia markets are being throttled by visa tightening and geopolitics.
technical_read: Not pulled -- stock is near its 52-week low, roughly 55% below its post-IPO high.
sentiment_summary: Read the entire thread (all 8 posts, 6 substantive), Feb-Aug 2026. It was started by himanshu.dugar (trusted, elevated-tier -- a SEBI-registered RA) with his IPO-era thesis. Later posts are thin: sanketkulkarni1987 flags unspecified governance red flags he wants to dig into; Prateek_Jha (Aug 2026) relays management guidance that FY27 will be flattish on the Middle-East crisis and US anti-immigrant policy, and notes there is no margin-expansion lever so sales growth is the only driver. No disagreement, but also no fresh bull conviction.

bull_case: Elite, asset-light economics: ~57% ROE, ~76% ROCE, debt-free, ~Rs 467 Cr net cash, ~4.7% dividend yield
Dominant B2B position in a structurally growing long-term market (Indian/global outbound students), 170+ university relationships
Trading near a 52-week low at a far lower multiple than at IPO -- if the visa cycle turns, growth and the multiple could re-rate together
bear_case: Management has guided FY27 to flat growth -- the core UK/Canada/Australia student-visa regimes are all tightening
No margin lever: ~70% of revenue is a contractual agent pass-through, so the stock is entirely a volume/growth story
Concentration on UK universities and on an agent network; unspecified governance questions raised on the thread
A high-ROE compounder with zero growth de-rates -- the quality ratios do not protect the price
verdict_headline: Superb economics, stalled engine -- a flat-guided growth story does not clear the 10x/100x bar
verdict_reasoning: thesis_fit neither: at ~Rs 3,000 Cr with management itself guiding FY27 flat, there is no supportable path to 10x in 2-3 years or ~47%+ sustained CAGR for 100x in 10 years
The recent-inflection rule cuts against this name, not for it -- the most recent data point is explicit deceleration to zero growth plus a structural (visa-policy) rather than transient cause
First-time pass; no red-flag tier (governance concerns raised but unsubstantiated); no active trusted conviction call -- floor not applicable

Conviction Low. Genuinely worth a revisit only if two things appear together: a visible turn in UK/Canada student-visa policy and a return to >20% revenue growth. Re-check trigger: FY27 H1 results showing growth resuming.
